summary:
Parses `str` using format `fmt`. The format can contain literal strings separated by %d (or %x) and %s specifiers. Each %d and %s corresponds in order to a destination argument var1, var2, and so on. %d reads an integer and %s reads a string. A * in a specifier, such as %*d or %*s, skips the corresponding input without assigning it.

LPC sscanf() resembles the C function but differs in several ways. Ordinary destination variables do not require the C address-of operator &. In LPC, sscanf(str, "%s %s",  str1,  str2) assigns the first word to str1 and the remainder to str2; in C, str2 would receive only the second word. The format %s%s cannot be used.

Returns the number of matched format specifiers.

Specifiers:
       %s          -   match a string
       %d          -   match an integer
       %f          -   match a float
       %x          -   match a base 16 number and convert to base 10
       %(regexp)   -   match a regexp pattern

   The "*" may be used in a specifier (e.g. "%*s") to skip over a match in
   the input string and not assign it to a function argument.   A "%%" may
   be used to match the "%" character,  which will also be skipped over in
   the function arguments.
